messages.subject: Fixing detection at 100% for colext
messages.body_plain:
Dear Unmarked community,
    First off, thanks for making such an awesome package that makes it easy for field ecologists to get meaningful answers to our questions.

       I am trying to analyze an occupancy 4 year dataset on Daurian Pika from Mongolia (a species with few published studies) with data from 2019, 2021, 2022, and 2025. We measure occupancy by checking every burrow entrance within a plot for fresh green scat, and have estimated detection probability around 100%. My main question is:

Using function colext, is there a way to fix detection probability at 1, and does this interfere with estimation of other parameters?

Secondary Question: From reading other posts on missing years in dynamic occupancy models, it looks like I can fit these open models with covariates and get good results for them, but the interpretation of the rates (say of extinction and colonization) are messy. Is this close to the correct interpretation?

Thanks,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Fixing detection at 100% with colext
messages.body_plain:
Dear Chris,

I assume that you don't have any replicate observations per site-year combination, right ?

Unfortunately, in unmarked there is no way to fix a parameter at a certain value such as 0 or 1. (Personally, I'd think this would be quite useful, but of course I have no clue about how hard this would be to implement !). You can, however, trick unmarked into fixing p at 1 by duplicating your detection data, so that instead of having a 0 you then have 0-0 and instead of a 1 you have 1-1. Since you then never have a "mixed" detection history per site-year combo, this makes unmarked believe that detection is perfect. You will change likelihood values etc, but for inference relative changes in the likelihood are all that counts, therefore,  I don't think that this is a problem.
To be honest, I am not sure how unmarked deals with missing primary periods in the context of this model fitting function. You could try to supply the data set with all-NA data filled in at the missing years and that would probably work (it would definitely work with a Bayesian analysis with JAGS and NIMBLE).

Best wishes -- Marc

messages.subject: error with modavg() and colext models
messages.subject_clean: error with modavg() and colext models
messages.body_plain:
I am seeing a new error with R ver. 4.5.1 when using modavg() to compute model averaged parameter estimates from a set of colext() models.  Here is example code from the modavg help page that now throws the error:
---------
library(AICcmodavg) # ver. 2.3-4
require(unmarked) # ver. 1.5.1

data(frogs)
umf <- formatMult(masspcru)
obsCovs(umf) <- scale(obsCovs(umf))
siteCovs(umf) <- rnorm(numSites(umf))
yearlySiteCovs(umf) <- data.frame(year = factor(rep(1:7,
                                    numSites(umf))))

fm <- colext(psiformula = ~ 1, gammaformula = ~ 1, epsilonformula = ~ 1,
             pformula = ~ JulianDate + I(JulianDate^2), data = umf,
             control = list(trace=1, maxit=1e4))

fm.yearly <- colext(psiformula = ~ 1, gammaformula = ~ year,
                    epsilonformula = ~ year,
                    pformula = ~ JulianDate + I(JulianDate^2),
                    data = umf)

Cand.mods <- list(fm, fm.yearly)
Modnames <- c("psi1(.)gam(.)eps(.)p(Date + Date2)",
              "psi1(.)gam(Year)eps(Year)p(Date + Date2)")

modavg(cand.set = Cand.mods, modnames = Modnames, parm = "(Intercept)",
       parm.type = "psi")
# Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
#   no slot of name "psiformula" for this object of class "unmarkedFitColExt"

modavg(cand.set = Cand.mods, modnames = Modnames,
       parm = "I(JulianDate^2)", parm.type = "detect")
# Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
#   no slot of name "detformula" for this object of class "unmarkedFitColExt"
---------
Thanks for any advice,
Scott P.

Chris Sutherland (he/him/his)

School of Mathematics and Statistics
University of St Andrews

W: website <https://www.sutherlandecology.com/>

E: cs...@st-andrews.ac.uk

From: ISEC Conference <isec.statist...@gmail.com>
Sent: 15 October 2025 04:01
To: ISEC Conference <isec.statist...@gmail.com>
Subject: ISEC 2027 in Mérida, México, January 8-15, 2027

(English:)

We are thrilled to announce that the next International Statistical Ecology Conference (ISEC) will be held in Mérida, México, on January 8-15, 2027, organized by the Autonomous University of Yucatán, and the Institute for Ecology and the Institute for Applied Mathematics and Systems Research from the National Autonomous University of México. ISEC is a biennial conference and serves as the main international gathering of statisticians and ecologists that work in the interdisciplinary field of statistical ecology. By closing the gap between ecology and statistics, two aims are achieved – helping ecologists discover new and state of the art statistical & machine learning methods and learn how best to use them, whilst at the same time make statisticians aware of the top priority methodological problems ecologists would like to solve.

The call for workshop proposals is now open. Previous 1-day and half-day workshops have covered R packages useful for the analysis of ecological data, animal movement modeling, generalized linear mixed models, generalized additive models, and Bayesian inference. We welcome similar workshop proposals that use R and/or Python, as well as those that focus on spatiotemporal models, eDNA, machine learning, artificial intelligence, computer vision, microbiome, and visualization of large data sets.

The call for roundtable proposals is also open. Roundtable discussions provide a platform to discuss important topics with other colleagues at ISEC. Some examples of possible roundtables: "The role of artificial intelligence in ecological data analysis", "Developing the statistical ecology community in México", "What topics should be included in a course on statistical ecology?".

The deadline for both is November 15, 2025, anywhere on Earth. For more information, visit statisticalecology.org <https://statisticalecology.org/>.

- Local Organizing Committee, ISEC 2027

(Español:)

Tenemos el agrado de anunciar que el próximo Congreso Internacional de Ecología Estadística (ISEC, por sus siglas en inglés) se llevará a cabo en Mérida, México, del 8 al 15 de enero de 2027. El evento será organizado por la Universidad Autónoma de Yucatán, en colaboración con el Instituto de Ecología y el Instituto de Investigaciones en Matemáticas Aplicadas y en Sistemas (IIMAS) de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México.

ISEC es un congreso bienal que funciona como el principal punto de encuentro internacional para estadísticos y ecólogos que trabajan en el campo interdisciplinario de la ecología estadística. Al cerrar la brecha entre la ecología y la estadística, se logran dos objetivos: ayudar a los ecólogos a descubrir métodos estadísticos y de aprendizaje automático (machine learning) nuevos y de vanguardia, y aprender cómo utilizarlos de la mejor manera posible; y, al mismo tiempo, hacer que los estadísticos conozcan los problemas metodológicos prioritarios que los ecólogos buscan resolver.

La convocatoria para propuestas de talleres ya está abierta. En años anteriores, se han ofrecido talleres de medio día o de un día completo sobre paqueterías de R útiles para el análisis de datos ecológicos, modelado de movimiento animal, modelos lineales generalizados mixtos, modelos aditivos generalizados e inferencia bayesiana. Se reciben con gusto propuestas de talleres similares que utilicen R y/o Python, así como aquellos que se enfoquen en modelos espaciotemporales, ADN ambiental (eDNA), aprendizaje automático, inteligencia artificial, visión por computadora, microbioma y visualización de grandes conjuntos de datos.

También está abierta la convocatoria para propuestas de mesas redondas. Las mesas redondas ofrecen un espacio para discutir temas importantes con otros colegas durante ISEC. Algunos ejemplos de posibles mesas redondas incluyen: “El papel de la inteligencia artificial en el análisis de datos ecológicos”, “Desarrollando la comunidad de ecología estadística en México”, “¿Qué temas deberían incluirse en un curso de ecología estadística?”.

La fecha límite para enviar propuestas para ambas convocatorias es el 15 de noviembre de 2025 (en cualquier lugar del mundo). Para más información, visita statisticalecology.org <https://statisticalecology.org/>

messages.subject: FormatDistData() question
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm working with a point count data set that is organized as row-per-detection.  I'm using the FormatDistData() function to organize the detections for analysis.  In addition to distance, the data set also has a column for "count", to record multiple individuals detected together. Rows mostly have a count of 1 but occasionally the value is higher to represent flocks of birds etc.
Is there a way to incorporate the values in the "count" column into my call to FormatDistData()?
Thanks!
-Tom

--
Tom McLaren
(he/him)
Biologist
Point Count Program
Klamath Bird Observatory <https://klamathbird.org/>

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] FormatDistData() question
messages.body_plain:
hi Tom,
 I'm afraid formatDistData does not accommodate that situation. But more importantly, the models in unmarked DO NOT accommodate non-independent detections so you should be careful with that.
 Having group detections is complicated because you might have to model group-size dependent detection and _also_ imperfect counting of group size so more complex models are needed. There are some Bayesian analysis papers out there on that (including in the AHM1 book, chapter 9).  Also of course Program Distance should handle these situations.
regards
andy

messages.subject: Distsamp; Error when fitting detection covariate
messages.subject_clean: Distsamp; Error when fitting detection covariate
messages.body_plain:
Hi unmarked community,

I first would like to thank everyone for posting and collaborating to keep this community active, as I have received a lot of help in my analysis browsing these pages.

Brief overview of my research and analysis: I am using distance sampling to estimate the abundance Paddlefish counted on side scan sonar images. We find that the pelagic nature of Paddlefish causes the detection probability of these creatures on sonar to decrease as distance from the boat increases, and distsamp is showing promise in determining the abundance of these animals in this way.

My problem: I hypothesize that the depth of the water affects the sonar image quality in the extremely deep parts of the lakes we are surveying (>15m) and subsequently I believe that the distortion of the sonar image may decrease our ability to detect Paddlefish in these areas. In order to better understand this, I am attempting to fit models where the (mean_depth) of each transect is used as a detection covariate and/or an abundance covariate (in the case Paddlefish distribution is affected by depth). What I have found is that all four keyfun fit when Mean_depth is an abundance covariate, however I receive the error "Error in .local(x, ...) : This method only works when there are no detection covars" when trying to fit mean_depth as a detection covariate using exp, halfnormal, and hazard key functions. Has anyone encountered this issue/ know where I am going wrong? I apologize if there is a simple reason why this is not working, as I am a novice user and not very good at math. Below is an excerpt of some of my models.

exp1<-distsamp(~1~1, umf, keyfun="exp", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
halfnorm1<-distsamp(~1~1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
hazard1<-distsamp(~1~1, umf, keyfun="hazard", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
uniform1<-distsamp(~1~1, umf, keyfun="uniform", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
exp_wDepth4abund<-distsamp(~1~Mean_Depth_m, umf, keyfun="exp", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
halfnorm_wDepth4abund<-distsamp(~1~Mean_Depth_m, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
hazard_wDepth4abund<-distsamp(~1~Mean_Depth_m, umf, keyfun="hazard", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
uniform_wDepth4abund<-distsamp(~1~Mean_Depth_m, umf, keyfun="uniform", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
exp_wDepth4det<-distsamp(~Mean_Depth_m~1, umf, keyfun="exp", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
halfnorm_wDepth4det<-distsamp(~Mean_Depth_m~1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
hazard_wDepth4det<-distsamp(~Mean_Depth_m~1, umf, keyfun="hazard", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)
uniform_wDepth4det<-distsamp(~Mean_Depth_m~1, umf, keyfun="uniform", output="density",unitsOut="ha", se=TRUE)

Thank You,

Wyatt Wolfenkoehler
Natural Resource Ecology and Management Graduate Research Assistant
Ok State Student Sub Unit AFS Vice President

messages.body_plain:
Hi Wyatt,

Normally this error occurs only when you run the hist() function on a fitted distance sampling model that contains covariates on detection. This is normal - the function is currently just limited that way, it doesn't mean there's something wrong the model.

Are you actually getting this error when fitting the model, i.e., does the error appear specifically right after you run the line of code containing 'distsamp()'? Or is it possible you have another line of code that runs hist() after fitting the model?

Ken
